name: New Kodo - Green
summary: Offered by Harb Clawhoof at Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore, this exchange allows seasoned riders to trade their aging Green Kodo for a fresh mount from the newer herd. It provides tauren and Horde champions an opportunity to ride a great brown, gray or white kodo across Kalimdor.

sections.title: A New Generation of Kodos
sections.body: Tauren rely on the powerful kodo beasts of Mulgore for labor, travel, and warfare. Breeding and caring for these enormous creatures requires steady patience and deep respect for the Earthmother's gifts. At Bloodhoof Village, breeder Harb Clawhoof tends to the corral, overseeing fresh stock raised to endure long marches across Kalimdor's rugged plains.

sections.title: The Exchange
sections.body: Over time, beasts of burden grow weary, and older mounts may be retired in favor of younger, spirited animals. Harb Clawhoof offers seasoned riders the chance to bring forth their older green kodos and swap them for a newly trained great kodo, ensuring the rider remains mounted on a creature fit for the trials facing the Horde.

faq.q: What is the purpose of this trade?
faq.answer: Harb Clawhoof allows owners of an older Green Kodo to exchange it for a beast from the newly raised herd, a great brown, gray or white kodo, matching the speed and stamina of their previous mount while sporting a fresh appearance.
Harb Clawhoof, the kodo breeder and mount vendor stationed by the pens in Bloodhoof Village within Mulgore, manages the trade.

faq.q: Where does this trade take place?
faq.answer: The exchange takes place at the kodo pens in Bloodhoof Village, a tauren settlement located in central Mulgore, south of Thunder Bluff.

faq.q: Why are kodos so important to the tauren?
faq.answer: Kodos are hardy, massive herbivores native to central Kalimdor. Their incredible endurance and broad frames make them ideal companions for the physically imposing tauren, who require exceptionally sturdy mounts for both war and nomadic travel.

faq.q: Are the new kodos faster than the old ones?
faq.answer: No. Harb Clawhoof notes that the new kodos possess the exact same speed and endurance as the older beasts; the primary distinction is their refreshed vitality and the coloration of their hide.

faq.q: Can members of other Horde races obtain this mount?
faq.answer: Tauren can acquire kodos naturally, while other members of the Horde must earn deep respect and exalted standing among the Thunder Bluff tauren before Harb Clawhoof will trust them with one of their prized beasts.

angles.text: Tending and riding kodos is an ancient tauren tradition, reflecting a lifelong bond with the spirits and wildlife of Mulgore.
Sturdy mounts are vital for coordinating defenses across the vast frontiers of the Barrens, Mulgore, and Durotar.
